hypothesis: A one-step perturbation of one symmetric coefficient in the verified n=5 prior-art candidate may preserve complete-circle feasibility while repairing at least one of its three taxi violations.
rationale: The published n=5 candidate is the correct verified finite baseline. Its ten integer upper-triangular coefficients define a small, interpretable local neighborhood that has not been screened in this repository; testing the exact +/-1 neighborhood is a bounded way to probe whether the residual taxi violations are locally repairable before paying for taxi-scale evaluation.
expected_information_gain: Determines whether strict improvement is locally accessible in coefficient space around the count-3 prior-art structure, and identifies whether complete-circle feasibility is a sharp gate for this neighborhood.
method: Construct exactly 21 candidates: the published control plus each of the ten coefficient coordinates changed by -1 and +1, holding the n=5 index matrix fixed. Evaluate every candidate on every edge of the complete circle m=6 metric using the pinned canonical potential arithmetic and direct frozen inequality count. Taxi evaluation is permitted only for non-control candidates with zero complete-circle violations; if none pass, stop this experiment without taxi work.
metric: violations_k on all 6006 complete-circle edges; conditional taxi violations_k on the frozen 7,000,602-edge circle-taxi metric
metric_relation_to_true_objective: Complete-circle feasibility is a necessary finite gate, not the true target. The frozen taxi count is the primary finite objective and must be below 3 for strict improvement; no finite count proves the full k-server conjecture.

compute_budget.cpu: WSL2 direct canonical potential screen with eight workers; taxi follow-up only for eligible circle-feasible neighbors
compute_budget.memory_intent: bounded complete-circle screen and no unqualified taxi runs

kill_condition: Stop after the 21-candidate complete-circle screen, at 900 seconds, or at a precise runtime failure. Do not expand the neighborhood, change the matrix, or infer taxi improvement from circle results. If no non-control candidate passes the circle gate, close this bounded family and pause k-server.

baseline_comparison.expected_relation: the control remains the best verified finite result; no neighbor is a strict improvement

previous_best_comparison.expected_relation: all 20 neighbors regressed relative to the control and none reached the target

interpretation: The complete-circle screen found 11 gated non-control neighbors, but the direct frozen taxi count showed all 20 non-control neighbors regressed to at least 18 violations; the control remained at 3. No candidate reached the strict target, so the declared local n=5 coefficient-neighbor family is closed.
what_was_learned: The residual taxi violations of the verified n=5 prior-art candidate are not repaired by any single +/-1 perturbation of its ten symmetric coefficients while holding the published index matrix fixed. Complete-circle feasibility is insufficient to predict taxi performance in this neighborhood.
recommended_next_action: Pause k-server and do not expand this one-step coefficient neighborhood; resume only for a materially different structural mechanism or stronger external capability.
repetition_justification: This is not a repeat of the n=7 coefficient or index-matrix work: it evaluates the previously untested +/-1 coefficient neighborhood of the distinct published n=5 candidate.
